simple.meaning: קַרְסֹל (qarçôl) is a Hebrew word meaning “an ankle (as a protuberance or joint).” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: קַרְסֹל (H7166) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at 2 Samuel 22:37, with occurrences in 2 Samuel, Psalms.

simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in קַרְסֹל (H7166) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: קַרְסֹל (qarçôl) / H7166 is traced through 2 Samuel 22:37, Psalms 18:37 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.short: an ankle (as a protuberance or joint)
definitions.full: H7166. qarsol [ קַרְסֹל ] noun [ feminine Albr ZAW xvi (1896), 77 ] ankle (compare ᵑ9 ᵐ5 2Sam 22:37 ; = ל + קֶרֶס see Kö ii. 1, 121 ; plural suffix קַסֻלָּ֑י 22:37 = Psa 18:37 ).

occurrences.englishText: You have enlarged my steps under me.
I will pursue my enemies, and overtake them.
